title: 대수기하학 원론 (EGA) — 한국어 누적판 / Éléments de géométrie algébrique — Korean Cumulative Edition
description:
Éléments de géométrie algébrique — Korean Cumulative Edition (대수기하학 원론 (EGA) — 한국어 누적판), release 2026-09-07-r48.

This front-facing reader contains every Korean EGA passage admitted so far by exact source, translation, typesetting, and deterministic validation gates: complete Korean EGA 0_I and EGA I; the complete EGA II Chapter II programme and table of contents; and one uninterrupted EGA II main-text translation through §2.5.12, canonical French source ega2-1-fr.tex lines 1–2694. The reader has 249 A4 pages and preserves 238 historical source-page boundaries. EGA II and the complete EGA corpus remain unfinished; the next source begins after blank line 2695 at Proposition 2.5.13 on line 2696. This release therefore makes no corpus-completion claim.

The r48 increment admits the already-prepared contiguous R40–R48 material in one source-ordered batch, extending the public reader from §2.2.6 to §2.5.12. Its substantive mathematics covers the homogeneous prime spectrum; its topology and standard opens; the scheme structure on Proj(S); functorial constructions from graded rings; local descriptions on D_+(f); sheaves associated with graded modules; twists; quasicoherence; and the canonical morphisms and local identifications needed for these constructions. Formula order, environments, labels, references, terminology decisions, and historical page markers remain bound to exact French source slices and Korean candidate hashes. A forward reference to §7.4.14 is deliberately retained as plain text because that later destination is not yet translated; no false PDF target is fabricated.

The cumulative Korean EGA II target is 124,497 UTF-8 bytes / 2,752 LF characters / SHA-256 6DE19B9A783DD17AFEE9C5DA36F29CB6A9F63C57768A4727281B7642C2914C03. Its admitted canonical French prefix is 118,946 bytes / SHA-256 04113B8FFC608C7CA286A77C37363C651C7AF529804C25B3BE519023A31B9F23. The cumulative PDF is 1,542,495 bytes / SHA-256 668E8008D24C5B676D18BCA933D3DD57159877F2B45BD778EA1CE28204A4623E. One mutex-held four-pass XeLaTeX convergence cycle produced byte-identical pass-3 and pass-4 PDFs. One aggregate whole-reader QA—never a per-section loop—checked all 17 Korean inputs, all 23 canonical driver rows, 1,134 labels, 1,509 source hyperlinks with zero missing targets, 654 PDF destinations, 1,735 link annotations, two independent text extractions, embedded fonts, A4 geometry, and focused 200-dpi renders of all twelve newly affected physical pages. No observed clipping, overlap, tofu, black boxes, damaged formula or diagram, unreadable text, replacement character, fatal TeX diagnostic, or unresolved link survived.

The stable Korean-edition DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.21921513; exact immutable r48 DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.22645017. The reinstated public working repository is github.com/KokunoYumeto/ega-ko. The preceding exact r39 DOI, 10.5281/zenodo.22416007, remains immutable history. Editable TeX, a fail-closed cumulative coverage matrix, source and terminology evidence, extraction inventories, renders, build logs, and SHA-256 manifests accompany the reader so that later corrections and extensions remain auditable and reproducible.

These checks are held hard against error, but establish only the tested properties. This independent translation is not a critical edition and makes no claim of perfection, infallibility, finality, external human certification, or endorsement. Legacy Type1 mathematics fonts do not provide lossless extraction; editable TeX and rendered formulae remain authoritative. Confirmed errors and documented uncertainties are corrected in later immutable versions without rewriting prior release evidence.

Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné are the historical creators. AI typesetting & translation is the sole standardized project contributor. The historical authors, NUMDAM, IHÉS, publishers, repositories, and cited third parties do not endorse this independently maintained Korean edition.

CC BY 4.0 applies only where the project holds the relevant rights: the Korean translation and typesetting, and project-authored metadata, indexes, decisions, and QA evidence. It makes no blanket public-domain or open-license claim for the underlying mathematical work, historical French edition, NUMDAM files, bibliography, or third-party content. Each source retains its exact provenance, attribution, author/source relationship, rights, and licence status.
